applies_why: The judge is resolving a link collision over Matthew 1:16 between the defender's and challenger's chains, so K-C governs whether the weighing was chain-against-chain by footing.
quote: D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': I weighed reading it as requiring the judge's stated reason to compare the chains' footing versus reading it as allowing a verse-level ambiguity to decide the link. The judge's text uses the latter reading, while the rule requires the former.
why: The judge declares the link underdetermined from the isolated ambiguity of Matthew 1:16's egennēthē/hēs rather than weighing the competing chains against one another by footing as K-C requires.
